No commutativity or connectedness assumption is needed; the homomorphism is algebraic.

+# Compact Root Coherence
+
+## Abstract
+
+Compactness turns separate positive roots into one coherent rational homomorphism.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Positive roots and rational homomorphisms are equivalent).**
+
+$$\forall H: \operatorname{Type}(u), [\operatorname{Group}(H)] [\operatorname{TopologicalSpace}(H)] [\operatorname{IsTopologicalGroup}(H)] [\operatorname{T2Space}(H)] [\operatorname{CompactSpace}(H)] \forall h: H, {\forall n: \mathbb{N}, 0 < n \Rightarrow \exists x: H, x^{n} = h} \iff {\exists phi: \operatorname{MonoidHom}(\operatorname{Multiplicative}(\mathbb{Q}), H), \operatorname{phi}(\operatorname{ofAdd}(1)) = h}.$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/CompactRootCoherence.exists_all_positive_roots_iff_exists_rat_hom` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary compact Hausdorff topological group H and h in H, the existence of a positive n-th root of h for every positive natural n is equivalent to one algebraic homomorphism from the additive rationals, represented as Multiplicative Q, sending additive rational one to h, that is, phi(ofAdd(1:Q)) = h.
+
+The forward direction puts all H-valued functions indexed by Q into the compact product H^Q. Each finite set of rational coordinates has a nonempty closed constraint set: a single D-th root of h supplies the values, and denominator clearing makes the finite addition equations hold inside its cyclic subgroup. Compactness then supplies a point in every finite constraint set, which is a global homomorphism. Hausdorffness is used for the closed equalizers.
+
+The reverse direction uses the root phi(ofAdd(1/n)) and applies its power map. No topology on Q, continuity, connectedness, Lie structure, faithfulness, or commutativity of H is asserted.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/CompactRootCoherence.exists_all_positive_roots_iff_exists_rat_hom`

+# A finite counterexample to improved thermal recall convergence
+
+## Abstract
+
+Removing intermediate memory resets increases the permutation approximation error in a finite reduced protocol.
+
+The system has d levels and the memory has n levels. Joint states are real-valued functions on Fin d × Fin n. The source defines the two-level thermalisation in TR.tex lines 269–275, the sequential rounds and truncated protocol in lines 289–296, the memory reset in lines 305–312, and the composed protocols in lines 315–324. At infinite temperature each elementary step is the average of the two selected entries, and the memory starts uniformly.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Two-level averaging).**
+
+$$\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall a \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right),\; \forall b \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right),\; \forall v \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \forall x \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right),\; \operatorname{average}\left(a, b, v\right)\left(x\right) = \operatorname{if} ((x = a) \lor (x = b)) \operatorname{then} \frac{(v\left(a\right) + v\left(b\right))}{2} \operatorname{else} v\left(x\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.average` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+At infinite temperature, replace the values at two joint states a and b by their average and leave every other value unchanged. This is the infinite-temperature form of the source's two-level thermalisation (TR.tex lines 269–275).
+
+**Definition 1.2 (A sequential thermalisation block).**
+
+$$\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall i \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right),\; \forall j \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right),\; \forall v \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \operatorname{block}\left(n, i, j, v\right) = \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{foldl}\left(\operatorname{fun} (u: \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \mathbb{R}) \mapsto (\operatorname{fun} (k: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)) \mapsto (\operatorname{List}.\operatorname{foldl}\left(\operatorname{fun} (u: \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \mathbb{R}) \mapsto (\operatorname{fun} (l: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)) \mapsto (\operatorname{average}\left((i, k), (j, l), u\right))), u, \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{finRange}\left(n\right)\right))), v, \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{finRange}\left(n\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.block` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a transposition of system levels i and j, process every memory level k of i in increasing order; for each k, average it successively with every memory level l of j in increasing order. The nested list folds implement the N rounds and the N steps in each round described in TR.tex lines 289–296.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (A system state with uniform memory).**
+
+$$\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall p \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \operatorname{joint}\left(n, p\right) = \operatorname{mixtureJoint}\left(p\right)\left(\operatorname{Function}.\operatorname{const}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right), \operatorname{Function}.\operatorname{const}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), ((n : \mathbb{R}))^{-1}\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.joint` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Couple a system population p to a uniform memory. Each joint entry is p at its system level multiplied by the inverse of the real memory dimension, matching the infinite-temperature memory state in TR.tex lines 289–291 and 338.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Memory reset).**
+
+$$\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall v \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \operatorname{reset}\left(v\right) = \operatorname{joint}\left(n, \operatorname{marginal}\left(v\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.reset` (`✓ std3`).

+*Citation.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Sum a joint state over the memory coordinate to obtain the system marginal, then tensor that marginal with a uniform memory. This is the full memory thermalisation from TR.tex lines 305–308.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Output without intermediate resets).**
+
+$$\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall p \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \forall w \in \operatorname{List}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right)\right),\; \operatorname{truncatedOutput}\left(n, p, w\right) = \operatorname{marginal}\left(\operatorname{List}.\operatorname{foldl}\left(\operatorname{fun} (v: \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \mathbb{R}) \mapsto (\operatorname{fun} (z: \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right)) \mapsto (\operatorname{block}\left(n, z.1, z.2\right)\left(v\right))), \operatorname{joint}\left(n, p\right), w\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.truncatedOutput` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Start from the joint state and apply the blocks in the word successively, with no reset between blocks. Return the system marginal, corresponding to the truncated composite protocol in TR.tex lines 293–296 and 321–322.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Output with intermediate resets).**
+
+$$\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall p \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \forall w \in \operatorname{List}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right)\right),\; \operatorname{resetOutput}\left(n, p, w\right) = \operatorname{marginal}\left(\operatorname{List}.\operatorname{foldl}\left(\operatorname{fun} (v: \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \mathbb{R}) \mapsto (\operatorname{fun} (z: \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right)) \mapsto (\operatorname{reset}\left(\operatorname{block}\left(n, z.1, z.2\right)\left(v\right)\right))), \operatorname{joint}\left(n, p\right), w\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.resetOutput` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Start from the joint state and apply each block followed immediately by a memory reset. Return the final system marginal, corresponding to the reset protocol in TR.tex lines 309–322.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (Reduced neighbour word).**
+
+$$\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall p \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \forall w \in \operatorname{List}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right)\right),\; \operatorname{IsReducedNeighbourWord}\left(p, w\right) \Leftrightarrow (\forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; (n < \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{length}\left(w\right)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{let} z = w[n]; \operatorname{let} r = \operatorname{applySwaps}\left(p, \operatorname{List}.\operatorname{take}\left(n, w\right)\right); (z.1 < z.2) \land ((r\left(z.2\right) < r\left(z.1\right)) \land (\forall c \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right),\; \neg ((r\left(z.2\right) < r\left(c\right)) \land (r\left(c\right) < r\left(z.1\right)))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.IsReducedNeighbourWord` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A word is reduced and neighbour-admissible when every position exchanges an increasing pair of system indices that is adjacent in the current population order and whose two values remain in their original relative order. The current order is obtained by applying the preceding swaps to p. This formalizes the reduced neighbour-transposition condition in TR.tex lines 315–325.
+
+**Definition 1.8 (Improved convergence for reduced words).**
+
+$$\operatorname{claim} \Leftrightarrow (\forall d \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall p \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \to \mathbb{R},\; \forall w \in \operatorname{List}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right) \times \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right)\right),\; (0 < n) \Rightarrow ((\forall i \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right),\; 0 \le p\left(i\right)) \Rightarrow ((\sum_{i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right)} (p\left(i\right)) = (1 : \mathbb{R})) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{StrictAnti}\left(p\right)) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{IsReducedNeighbourWord}\left(p, w\right)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{totalVariation}\left(\operatorname{applySwaps}\left(p, w\right), \operatorname{truncatedOutput}\left(n, p, w\right)\right) \le \operatorname{totalVariation}\left(\operatorname{applySwaps}\left(p, w\right), \operatorname{resetOutput}\left(n, p, w\right)\right)))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).

+*Source.* Repository-derived.

+*Acknowledgement.* Jakub Czartowski; A. de Oliveira Junior; Kamil Korzekwa (2023). *Thermal Recall: Memory-Assisted Markovian Thermal Processes*. DOI: [10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.040304). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12840v2>.

+*Commentary.*
+
+For every positive memory dimension, nonnegative system population of total mass one, strictly decreasing population, and reduced neighbour word, the total variation distance from the ideal swapped population is no larger without intermediate resets than with them. This is the repository's formal reading of the improved-convergence conjecture stated in TR.tex lines 417–427.

+**Theorem 1.9 (A four-level counterexample).**
+
+$$\neg (\operatorname{claim})$$

+    exact List.take_prefix _ _
+  exact (show w <:+: p++w from ⟨p,[],by simp⟩).trans hp.isInfix
+

+/-- Source-selected paths imply a lower bound for the actual visible event against
+every measurable event of the complete marked past, including null hidden fibers. -/
+theorem original_rectangle_occurrence (θ : Presentation H)
+    (J : Measure (PathSpace H)) [IsProbabilityMeasure J] (hc : HasOriginalCylinders J θ)
+    (w : List Bool) (R : Rectangle (product θ w)) (r : H) (hr : r ∈ R.rows)
+    (a : ∀ h, LabelledRoute θ h r) (ha : ∀ h, (a h).length ≤ Fintype.card H) :
+    let ε := selectedEpsilon θ w r a
+    let b := w.length + Fintype.card H
+    0 < ε ∧ ε ≤ 1 ∧
+    (∀ (t : ℤ) (h : H), 0 < θ.initial h →
+      ENNReal.ofReal ε ≤ futureLaw J t h (success w b)) ∧
+    (∀ (t : ℤ) (h : H) (A : Set (ℕ → H × Bool)), MeasurableSet A →
+      ENNReal.ofReal ε * J ((state t ⁻¹' {h}) ∩ (past t ⁻¹' A)) ≤
+        J ((state t ⁻¹' {h}) ∩ (past t ⁻¹' A) ∩ (future t ⁻¹' success w b))) := by
+  dsimp only
+  let ε := selectedEpsilon θ w r a
+  let b := w.length + Fintype.card H
+  have hrow : 0 < ∑ j, product θ w r j := by
+    obtain ⟨j,hj⟩ := R.cols_nonempty
+    exact (R.positive r hr j hj).trans_le
+      (Finset.single_le_sum (fun k _ => product_nonneg θ w r k) (Finset.mem_univ j))
+  have hε : 0 < ε := by
+    apply (Finset.lt_inf'_iff _).mpr
+    intro h _
+    exact mul_pos (Finset.prod_pos fun i _ => (a h).positive i) hrow
+  have lower (t : ℤ) (h : H) (hi : 0 < θ.initial h) :
+      ENNReal.ofReal ε ≤ futureLaw J t h (success w b) := by
+    let p := List.ofFn (a h).labels
+    have hb : (p++w).length ≤ b := by
+      dsimp [p,b]
+      simpa only [List.length_append, List.length_ofFn, Nat.add_comm] using
+        Nat.add_le_add_right (ha h) w.length
+    have hm := futureLaw_readPrefix θ J hc t h hi (p++w).length (p++w).get
+    rw [Measure.map_apply (by unfold readPrefix; fun_prop) (measurableSet_singleton _)] at hm
+    calc
+      ENNReal.ofReal ε ≤ ENNReal.ofReal
+          (pathMass θ.matrix (a h).length (a h).states (a h).labels * ∑ j, product θ w r j) :=
+        ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (Finset.inf'_le _ (Finset.mem_univ h))
+      _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∑ j, product θ (p++w) h j) :=
+        ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (route_word_mass θ w r h (a h))
+      _ = futureLaw J t h (readPrefix (p++w).length ⁻¹' {(p++w).get}) := by
+        rw [hm]
+        congr 1
+        simp only [futureMass, ← product_word]
+      _ ≤ _ := measure_mono (prefix_success w p b hb)
+  have hsum : 0 < ∑ h, θ.initial h := by rw [θ.initial_sum]; norm_num
+  obtain ⟨h,_,hi⟩ := (Finset.sum_pos_iff_of_nonneg fun h _ => θ.initial_nonneg h).mp hsum
+  have hε1 : ε ≤ 1 := by
+    have hh := (lower 0 h hi).trans prob_le_one
+    exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_one).mp hh
+  refine ⟨hε,hε1,lower,?_⟩
+  intro t h A hA
+  by_cases hi : 0 < θ.initial h
+  · rw [full_past_future_factor θ J hc t h hi A (success w b) hA (success_measurable w b),
+      mul_comm (J _)]
+    exact mul_le_mul_left (lower t h hi) _
+  · have hz : θ.initial h = 0 := le_antisymm (le_of_not_gt hi) (θ.initial_nonneg h)
+    have hn : J (state t ⁻¹' {h}) = 0 := by
+      apply (ENNReal.toReal_eq_zero_iff _).mp ?_ |>.resolve_right (measure_ne_top _ _)
+      change J.real (state t ⁻¹' {h}) = 0
+      rw [state_mass θ J hc, hz]
+    have hn' : J ((state t ⁻¹' {h}) ∩ (past t ⁻¹' A)) = 0 :=
+      measure_mono_null Set.inter_subset_left hn
+    rw [hn',mul_zero]
+    exact zero_le
+

+/-- A prescribed hidden path after the cut, followed by an arbitrary output word,
+retains its exact path weight in the original marked-cylinder law. -/
+private theorem past_route_future_mass (θ : Presentation H) (J : Measure (PathSpace H))
+    [IsProbabilityMeasure J] (hc : HasOriginalCylinders J θ) (t : ℤ) (m n l : ℕ)
+    (h : Fin (m+1) → H) (w : Fin m → Bool) (k : Fin (n+1) → H)
+    (v : Fin n → Bool) (u : Fin l → Bool) (hk : k 0 = h (Fin.last m)) :
+    J.real (MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder (t-m) m h w ∩
+      MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder t n k v ∩
+      Prod.snd ⁻¹' visibleCylinder (t+n) l u) =
+      θ.initial (h 0) * pathMass θ.matrix m h w *
+        (pathMass θ.matrix n k v * futureMass θ.matrix (k (Fin.last n)) l u) := by
+  let g := joinHidden m n h (Fin.tail k)
+  have hg (i : Fin (n+1)) :
+      g ⟨m+i.val, by omega⟩ = k i := by
+    rw [show g = joinHidden m n h (Fin.tail k) from rfl, join_right, ← hk]
+    simp only [Fin.cons_self_tail]
+  have he : MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder (t-m) m h w ∩
+      MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder t n k v =
+      MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder (t-m) (m+n) g (Fin.append w v) := by
+    ext z
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨⟨hh,hw⟩,⟨hh',hv⟩⟩
+      constructor
+      · intro i
+        by_cases hi : i.val ≤ m
+        · exact (hh ⟨i.val, by omega⟩).trans (join_left m n h (Fin.tail k) ⟨i.val, by omega⟩).symm
+        · let j : Fin (n+1) := ⟨i.val-m, by omega⟩
+          have ht : t-(m:ℤ)+i.val = t+j.val := by dsimp [j]; omega
+          have hi' : i = ⟨m+j.val, by omega⟩ := by ext; dsimp [j]; omega
+          rw [ht,hi',hg]
+          exact hh' j
+      · intro i
+        refine Fin.addCases (fun j => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i
+        · simpa only [Fin.append_left, Fin.val_castAdd] using hw j
+        · rw [Fin.append_right]
+          simpa only [Fin.val_natAdd, Nat.cast_add, ← add_assoc, sub_add_cancel] using hv j
+    · rintro ⟨hh,hw⟩
+      constructor
+      · constructor
+        · intro i
+          exact (hh ⟨i.val, by omega⟩).trans (join_left m n h (Fin.tail k) i)
+        · intro i
+          simpa only [Fin.append_left, Fin.val_castAdd] using hw (Fin.castAdd n i)
+      · constructor
+        · intro i
+          have hh' := (hh ⟨m+i.val, by omega⟩).trans (hg i)
+          simpa only [Nat.cast_add, ← add_assoc, sub_add_cancel] using hh'
+        · intro i
+          have hw' := hw (Fin.natAdd m i)
+          rw [Fin.append_right] at hw'
+          simpa only [Fin.val_natAdd, Nat.cast_add, ← add_assoc, sub_add_cancel] using hw'
+  rw [he]
+  have hm := past_future_mass θ J hc (t+n) (m+n) l g (Fin.append w v) u
+  have ht : t+(n:ℤ)-(m+n:ℕ) = t-m := by push_cast; omega
+  rw [ht] at hm
+  have h0 : g 0 = h 0 := join_left m n h (Fin.tail k) 0
+  have hn : g (Fin.last (m+n)) = k (Fin.last n) := by
+    exact (congrArg g (Fin.ext rfl)).trans (hg (Fin.last n))
+  have hp : pathMass θ.matrix (m+n) g (Fin.append w v) =
+      pathMass θ.matrix m h w * pathMass θ.matrix n k v := by
+    rw [show g = joinHidden m n h (Fin.tail k) from rfl, path_concat, ← hk, Fin.cons_self_tail]
+  rw [h0,hn,hp] at hm
+  simpa only [mul_assoc] using hm

+/-- The particular selected hidden route followed by the specified visible word.
+All later coordinates, including the unused suffix of the block, are unrestricted. -/
+def routeWord (θ : Presentation H) (t : ℤ) {h r : H}
+    (a : LabelledRoute θ h r) (w : List Bool) : Set (PathSpace H) :=
+  MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder t a.length a.states a.labels ∩
+    Prod.snd ⁻¹' visibleCylinder (t+a.length) w.length w.get
+
+private theorem routeWord_measurable (θ : Presentation H) (t : ℤ) {h r : H}
+    (a : LabelledRoute θ h r) (w : List Bool) : MeasurableSet (routeWord θ t a w) :=
+  (cylinder_measurable _ _ _ _).inter ((show MeasurableSet
+    (visibleCylinder (t+a.length) w.length w.get) from by
+      unfold visibleCylinder
+      simp only [Set.ofPred_forall]
+      exact MeasurableSet.iInter fun i => (measurableSet_singleton _).preimage
+        (measurable_pi_apply _)).preimage measurable_snd)
+
+/-- Exact probability of the prescribed hidden route and word, tested against
+EVERY measurable complete marked-past event, rather than just finite cylinders. -/
+theorem route_word_past_factor (θ : Presentation H) (J : Measure (PathSpace H))
+    [IsProbabilityMeasure J] (hc : HasOriginalCylinders J θ) (t : ℤ) (h r : H)
+    (a : LabelledRoute θ h r) (w : List Bool) :
+    MeasurableSet (routeWord θ t a w) ∧
+    (∀ b : ℕ, a.length + w.length ≤ b → routeWord θ t a w ⊆ future t ⁻¹' success w b) ∧
+    (∀ A : Set (ℕ → H × Bool), MeasurableSet A →
+      J ((past t ⁻¹' A) ∩ routeWord θ t a w) =
+        J ((state t ⁻¹' {h}) ∩ (past t ⁻¹' A)) *
+          ENNReal.ofReal (pathMass θ.matrix a.length a.states a.labels * ∑ j, product θ w r j)) := by
+  refine ⟨routeWord_measurable θ t a w,?_,?_⟩
+  · intro b hb z hz
+    let p := List.ofFn a.labels
+    apply prefix_success w p b (by simpa [p] using hb)
+    change readPrefix (p++w).length (future t z) = (p++w).get
+    apply List.ofFn_injective
+    rw [List.ofFn_get]
+    apply List.ext_getElem
+    · simp
+    · intro k hk hk'
+      simp only [List.getElem_ofFn,readPrefix,future]
+      by_cases hka : k < a.length
+      · rw [List.getElem_append_left (by simpa [p] using hka)]
+        simpa only [p,List.getElem_ofFn] using hz.1.2 ⟨k,hka⟩
+      · rw [List.getElem_append_right (by simpa [p] using Nat.le_of_not_gt hka)]
+        have hkw : k-a.length < w.length := by
+          simp only [p,List.length_append,List.length_ofFn] at hk'
+          omega
+        have he := hz.2 ⟨k-a.length,hkw⟩
+        have ht : t+(k:ℤ) = t+(a.length:ℤ)+(k-a.length:ℕ) := by omega
+        simp only [p,List.length_ofFn]
+        change z.2 (t+(k:ℤ)) = w[k-a.length]
+        rw [ht]
+        exact he
+  intro A hA
+  let c := ENNReal.ofReal (pathMass θ.matrix a.length a.states a.labels * ∑ j, product θ w r j)
+  have hp : Measurable (past (H := H) t) := by unfold past; fun_prop
+  have hs : Measurable (state (H := H) t) := by unfold state; fun_prop
+  let μ := (J.restrict (routeWord θ t a w)).map (past t)
+  let ν := c • (J.restrict (state t ⁻¹' {h})).map (past t)
+  haveI : IsFiniteMeasure ν := Measure.smul_finite _ ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top
+  have he : μ = ν := by
+    apply NativeBorelCEvent.measure_eq_of_prefix
+    intro n
+    apply Measure.ext_of_singleton
+    intro p
+    let k : Fin (n+1+1) → H := Fin.snoc (fun i => (p i.rev).1) h
+    let v : Fin (n+1) → Bool := fun i => (p i.rev).2
+    let E := MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder (t-(n+1:ℕ)) (n+1) k v
+    have hr : Measurable (readPrefix (S := H × Bool) (n+1)) := by unfold readPrefix; fun_prop
+    change μ.map (readPrefix (n+1)) {p} = ν.map (readPrefix (n+1)) {p}
+    dsimp [μ,ν]
+    rw [Measure.map_map hr hp, Measure.map_apply (hr.comp hp) (measurableSet_singleton p),
+      Measure.restrict_apply ((measurableSet_singleton p).preimage (hr.comp hp)),
+      Measure.map_smul _ hr.aemeasurable, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
+      Measure.map_map hr hp, Measure.map_apply (hr.comp hp) (measurableSet_singleton p),
+      Measure.restrict_apply ((measurableSet_singleton p).preimage (hr.comp hp))]
+    have hsub : routeWord θ t a w ⊆ state t ⁻¹' {h} := by
+      intro z hz
+      change z.1 t = h
+      simpa only [Fin.val_zero, Nat.cast_zero, add_zero, a.first] using hz.1.1 0
+    have hi : (past t ⁻¹' (readPrefix (n+1) ⁻¹' {p})) ∩ routeWord θ t a w =
+        E ∩ routeWord θ t a w := by
+      rw [show E = (past t ⁻¹' (readPrefix (n+1) ⁻¹' {p})) ∩ (state t ⁻¹' {h}) from
+        (past_prefix_cylinder t (n+1) p h).symm]
+      ext z
+      exact ⟨fun hz => ⟨⟨hz.1,hsub hz.2⟩,hz.2⟩, fun hz => ⟨hz.1.1,hz.2⟩⟩
+    change J ((past t ⁻¹' (readPrefix (n+1) ⁻¹' {p})) ∩ routeWord θ t a w) =
+      c * J ((past t ⁻¹' (readPrefix (n+1) ⁻¹' {p})) ∩ (state t ⁻¹' {h}))
+    rw [hi, past_prefix_cylinder]
+    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_toReal (measure_ne_top J _)]
+    change ENNReal.ofReal (J.real _) = _
+    have hm := past_route_future_mass θ J hc t (n+1) a.length w.length k v a.states a.labels w.get
+      (by simpa [k] using a.first)
+    rw [show E ∩ routeWord θ t a w =
+      (MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder (t-(n+1:ℕ)) (n+1) k v ∩
+        MarkedPredictiveQuotient.cylinder t a.length a.states a.labels) ∩
+        Prod.snd ⁻¹' visibleCylinder (t+a.length) w.length w.get from Set.inter_assoc _ _ _ |>.symm]
+    rw [hm, a.last]
+    simp only [futureMass, ← product_word]
+    rw [ENNReal.ofReal_mul (mul_nonneg (θ.initial_nonneg _) (path_nonneg θ _ _ _))]
+    rw [← hc (t-(n+1:ℕ)) (n+1) k v]
+    change ENNReal.ofReal (J.real E) * c = c * J E
+    rw [measureReal_def, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal (measure_ne_top J _), mul_comm]
+  have ha := congrArg (fun ζ : Measure (ℕ → H × Bool) => ζ A) he
+  dsimp [μ,ν] at ha
+  simp only [Measure.map_apply hp hA, Measure.restrict_apply (hp hA),
+    Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at ha
+  simpa only [Set.inter_comm, mul_comm, c] using ha
+
+private theorem closed_stationary (θ : Presentation H) (C : Finset H)
+    (hclosed : ∀ (i : C) j, j ∉ C → ∀ x, θ.matrix x i.val j = 0) :
+    ∀ j : C, ∑ i : C, θ.initial i.val *
+      (θ.matrix false i.val j.val + θ.matrix true i.val j.val) = θ.initial j.val := by
+  have hs (i : C) : ∑ j : C, (θ.matrix false i.val j.val + θ.matrix true i.val j.val) = 1 := by
+    rw [Finset.sum_coe_sort _ (fun j : H => θ.matrix false i.val j + θ.matrix true i.val j)]
+    calc
+      _ = ∑ j, (θ.matrix false i.val j + θ.matrix true i.val j) := by
+        apply Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ _)
+        intro j _ hj
+        rw [hclosed i j hj false,hclosed i j hj true,add_zero]
+      _ = 1 := θ.stochastic i.val
+  have hl (j : C) : (∑ i : C, θ.initial i.val *
+      (θ.matrix false i.val j.val + θ.matrix true i.val j.val)) ≤ θ.initial j.val := by
+    rw [←θ.stationary j.val,Finset.sum_coe_sort C (fun i : H => θ.initial i * (θ.matrix false i j.val + θ.matrix true i j.val))]
+    exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _) fun i _ _ =>
+      mul_nonneg (θ.initial_nonneg _) (add_nonneg (θ.matrix_nonneg _ _ _) (θ.matrix_nonneg _ _ _))
+  have ht : (∑ j : C, ∑ i : C, θ.initial i.val *
+      (θ.matrix false i.val j.val + θ.matrix true i.val j.val)) = ∑ j : C, θ.initial j.val := by
+    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+    simp_rw [←Finset.mul_sum,hs,mul_one]
+  intro j
+  exact (Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le (fun j _ => hl j)).mp ht j (Finset.mem_univ j)
+
+private theorem weighted_no11 (θ : Presentation H) (i j : H) :
+    θ.initial i * (θ.matrix true*θ.matrix true) i j = 0 := by
+  by_cases hi : 0 < θ.initial i
+  · rw [PositiveSupportPresentation.weighted_no11 θ ⟨i, hi⟩ j, mul_zero]
+  · rw [le_antisymm (le_of_not_gt hi) (θ.initial_nonneg i), zero_mul]
+
+/-- The actual restriction to a positive-weight closed class, with normalized
+original stationary masses and unchanged original real matrix entries. -/
+def nativeComponent (θ : Presentation H)
+    (C : FiniteClosedClasses.ClosedClass (θ.matrix false+θ.matrix true))
+    (hc : 0 < ∑ i : C.val, θ.initial i.val) : Presentation C.val := by
+  let T := θ.matrix false+θ.matrix true
+  have hT : T ∈ rowStochastic ℝ H := Matrix.mem_rowStochastic_iff_sum.mpr
+    ⟨fun i j => add_nonneg (θ.matrix_nonneg _ _ _) (θ.matrix_nonneg _ _ _),θ.stochastic⟩
+  have hclosed (i : C.val) (j : H) (hj : j ∉ C.val) (x : Bool) : θ.matrix x i.val j = 0 := by
+    have hz := (FiniteClosedClasses.actual_structure T hT).class_no_exit C 1 i j hj
+    change (T^1) i.val j = 0 at hz
+    simp only [pow_one] at hz
+    change θ.matrix false i.val j + θ.matrix true i.val j = 0 at hz
+    cases x <;> linarith [θ.matrix_nonneg false i.val j,θ.matrix_nonneg true i.val j]
+  let c : ℝ := ∑ i : C.val, θ.initial i.val
+  refine { initial := fun i => θ.initial i.val/c
+           matrix := fun x i j => θ.matrix x i.val j.val
+           initial_nonneg := fun i => div_nonneg (θ.initial_nonneg _) hc.le
+           initial_sum := ?_
+           matrix_nonneg := fun x i j => θ.matrix_nonneg _ _ _
+           stochastic := ?_
+           stationary := ?_
+           no11 := ?_ }
+  · rw [←Finset.sum_div]
+    exact div_self (ne_of_gt hc)
+  · intro i
+    rw [Finset.sum_coe_sort _ (fun j : H => θ.matrix false i.val j + θ.matrix true i.val j)]
+    calc
+      _ = ∑ j, (θ.matrix false i.val j + θ.matrix true i.val j) := by
+        apply Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ _)
+        intro j _ hj
+        rw [hclosed i j hj false,hclosed i j hj true,add_zero]
+      _ = 1 := θ.stochastic i.val
+  · intro j
+    simp_rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div]
+    rw [←Finset.sum_div,closed_stationary θ C.val hclosed j]
+  · apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+    intro i _
+    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+    intro j _
+    have hp : (∑ k : C.val, θ.matrix true i.val k.val * θ.matrix true k.val j.val) =
+        (θ.matrix true*θ.matrix true) i.val j.val := by
+      rw [Matrix.mul_apply,Finset.sum_coe_sort _ (fun k : H => θ.matrix true i.val k * θ.matrix true k j.val)]
+      apply Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ _)
+      intro k _ hk
+      rw [hclosed i k hk true,zero_mul]
+    have hz := weighted_no11 θ i.val j.val
+    change θ.initial i.val / c * (∑ k : C.val, θ.matrix true i.val k.val * θ.matrix true k.val j.val) = 0
+    rw [hp,div_mul_eq_mul_div,hz,zero_div]
+
+/-- Inclusion of an actual hidden component preserves the original output clock. -/
+def componentInclusion (C : Finset H) (z : PathSpace C) : PathSpace H :=
+  (fun t => (z.1 t).val, z.2)
+
+private theorem componentInclusion_measurable (C : Finset H) :
+    Measurable (componentInclusion (H := H) C) := by
+  exact (Measurable.of_eval fun t => measurable_subtype_coe.comp
+    ((measurable_pi_apply t).comp measurable_fst)).prodMk measurable_snd
+
+private theorem window_domination {S : Type*} [Fintype S] [MeasurableSpace S]
+    [MeasurableSingletonClass S] (μ ν : Measure (ℤ → S))
+    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
+    (h : ∀ (t : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (w : Fin (n+1) → S),
+      μ.real ((fun x (i : Fin (n+1)) => x (t+i.val)) ⁻¹' {w}) ≤
+      ν.real ((fun x (i : Fin (n+1)) => x (t+i.val)) ⁻¹' {w})) : μ ≤ ν := by
+  classical
+  have hC (C : Set (ℤ → S)) (hC : C ∈ measurableCylinders (fun _ : ℤ => S)) :
+      μ.real C ≤ ν.real C := by
+    obtain ⟨I,T,hT,he⟩ := (mem_measurableCylinders C).mp hC
+    let n : ℕ := I.sup Int.natAbs
+    let window : (ℤ → S) → (Fin (2*n+1) → S) := fun z k => z (-(n:ℤ)+k.val)
+    let select : (Fin (2*n+1) → S) → ((i : I) → S) := fun w i =>
+      w ⟨(i.val+(n:ℤ)).toNat,by
+        have hi := Finset.le_sup (f := Int.natAbs) i.property
+        have hab := Int.natAbs_eq i.val
+        omega⟩
+    let U : Finset (Fin (2*n+1) → S) := Finset.univ.filter (fun w => select w ∈ T)
+    have hread : I.restrict = select ∘ window := by
+      funext z i
+      have hi := Finset.le_sup (f := Int.natAbs) i.property
+      have hab := Int.natAbs_eq i.val
+      change z i.val = z (-(n:ℤ)+((i.val+(n:ℤ)).toNat:ℤ))
+      congr 1
+      omega
+    have hset : C = window ⁻¹' (U : Set (Fin (2*n+1) → S)) := by
+      rw [he]
+      change (I.restrict : (ℤ → S) → (I → S)) ⁻¹' T = _

+/- GID: D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation

+   utility: kind=certified-instance; basis=refutes=gid:D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.claim; result=D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.result; claim=D5/S3/StatisticalMechanics/ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation.claim
+   digest: Removing intermediate memory resets can increase permutation approximation error. -/
+
+import D5.S3.Combinatorics.Permutation.AdamsonFlahertyPotapovSpirakisTwoSwapGreedy
+import D5.S3.Entropy.Mixing.MixtureEntropyBracket
+import D5.S3.TotalVariation.CycleSingleCutMinimax
+
+/-! Finite thermalisation protocols with and without intermediate memory resets. -/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option linter.style.longLine false
+
+namespace D5.S3.StatisticalMechanics.ThermalRecallTruncationRefutation
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+open D5.S3.Combinatorics.Permutation.AdamsonFlahertyPotapovSpirakisTwoSwapGreedy
+  (applySwaps)
+open D5.S3.Divergence.ChainRule (marginal)
+open D5.S3.Entropy.Mixing.MixtureEntropyBracket (mixtureJoint)
+open D5.S3.TotalVariation.Pinsker
+open D5.S3.TotalVariation.CycleSingleCutMinimax (Probability)
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- Two-level thermalisation at infinite temperature. -/
+def average {d n : ℕ} (a b : Fin d × Fin n)
+    (v : Fin d × Fin n → ℝ) : Fin d × Fin n → ℝ :=
+  fun x => if x = a ∨ x = b then (v a + v b) / 2 else v x
+
+/-- Rounds increase the first memory index; steps increase the second memory index. -/
+def block {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin d)
+    (v : Fin d × Fin n → ℝ) : Fin d × Fin n → ℝ :=
+  (List.finRange n).foldl
+    (fun u k => (List.finRange n).foldl (fun u l => average (i, k) (j, l) u) u) v
+
+/-- Couple a system population vector to a uniform memory. -/
+def joint {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (p : Fin d → ℝ) : Fin d × Fin n → ℝ :=
+  mixtureJoint p (fun (_ : Fin d) (_ : Fin n) => (n : ℝ)⁻¹)
+
+/-- Reset the memory to its uniform infinite-temperature state. -/
+def reset {d n : ℕ} (v : Fin d × Fin n → ℝ) : Fin d × Fin n → ℝ :=
+  joint n (marginal v)
+
+/-- Composite protocol with the intermediate resets removed, read on the system. -/
+def truncatedOutput {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (p : Fin d → ℝ)
+    (w : List (Fin d × Fin d)) : Fin d → ℝ :=
+  marginal (w.foldl (fun v z => block n z.1 z.2 v) (joint n p))
+
+/-- Composite protocol with a memory reset after every block. -/
+def resetOutput {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (p : Fin d → ℝ)
+    (w : List (Fin d × Fin d)) : Fin d → ℝ :=
+  marginal (w.foldl (fun v z => reset (block n z.1 z.2 v)) (joint n p))
+
+/-- Each swap is adjacent in current population order and increases inversion length. -/
+def IsReducedNeighbourWord {d : ℕ} (p : Fin d → ℝ) : List (Fin d × Fin d) → Prop :=
+  fun w => ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n < w.length),
+    let z := w[n]
+    let r := applySwaps p (w.take n)
+    z.1 < z.2 ∧ r z.2 < r z.1 ∧ ∀ c, ¬ (r z.2 < r c ∧ r c < r z.1)
+
+/-- Improved convergence of the truncated protocol for every reduced neighbour word. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ (d n : ℕ) (p : Fin d → ℝ) (w : List (Fin d × Fin d)),
+    0 < n → (∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) → ∑ i, p i = 1 → StrictAnti p →
+    IsReducedNeighbourWord p w →
+    totalVariation (applySwaps p w) (truncatedOutput n p w) ≤
+      totalVariation (applySwaps p w) (resetOutput n p w)
+
+private def p : Fin 4 → ℝ := ![1/2, 1/4, 2/9, 1/36]
+
+private def w : List (Fin 4 × Fin 4) := [(0, 1), (2, 3), (0, 3)]
+
+private theorem instance_hypotheses :
+    Probability p ∧ StrictAnti p ∧ IsReducedNeighbourWord p w := by
+  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro i
+    fin_cases i <;> norm_num [p.eq_1]
+  · norm_num [p.eq_1, Fin.sum_univ_four]
+  · intro i j hij
+    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> norm_num [p.eq_1] at *
+  · intro k hk
+    have hk' : k < 3 := hk
+    change
+      let z := w[k]
+      let r := (w.take k).foldl (fun r z => r ∘ Equiv.swap z.1 z.2) p
+      z.1 < z.2 ∧ r z.2 < r z.1 ∧ ∀ c, ¬ (r z.2 < r c ∧ r c < r z.1)
+    interval_cases k <;>
+      norm_num [w.eq_1, p.eq_1, Function.comp_apply,
+        Equiv.swap_apply_def, Fin.forall_fin_succ]
+
+private theorem target_values : applySwaps p w = ![2/9, 1/2, 1/36, 1/4] := by
+  change w.foldl (fun r z => r ∘ Equiv.swap z.1 z.2) p = _
+  funext i
+  fin_cases i <;>
+    norm_num [p.eq_1, w.eq_1, Function.comp_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_def]
+
+private theorem joint_values :
+    joint 2 p = fun x => ![![1/4, 1/4], ![1/8, 1/8], ![1/9, 1/9], ![1/72, 1/72]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  change p i / 2 = _
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;> norm_num [p.eq_1]
+
+private theorem truncated_block_one :
+    block 2 0 1 (fun x => ![![1/4, 1/4], ![1/8, 1/8], ![1/9, 1/9], ![1/72, 1/72]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![5/32, 3/16], ![7/32, 3/16], ![1/9, 1/9], ![1/72, 1/72]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  change (List.finRange 2).foldl
+      (fun (u : Fin 4 × Fin 2 → ℝ) k => (List.finRange 2).foldl
+        (fun u l x => if x = (0, k) ∨ x = (1, l) then
+          (u (0, k) + u (1, l)) / 2 else u x) u) _ = _
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;>
+    norm_num [List.finRange_succ, List.finRange_zero]
+
+private theorem truncated_block_two :
+    block 2 2 3 (fun x => ![![5/32, 3/16], ![7/32, 3/16], ![1/9, 1/9], ![1/72, 1/72]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![5/32, 3/16], ![7/32, 3/16], ![11/288, 1/16], ![25/288, 1/16]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  change (List.finRange 2).foldl
+      (fun (u : Fin 4 × Fin 2 → ℝ) k => (List.finRange 2).foldl
+        (fun u l x => if x = (2, k) ∨ x = (3, l) then
+          (u (2, k) + u (3, l)) / 2 else u x) u) _ = _
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;>
+    norm_num [List.finRange_succ, List.finRange_zero]
+
+private theorem truncated_block_three :
+    block 2 0 3 (fun x => ![![5/32, 3/16], ![7/32, 3/16], ![11/288, 1/16], ![25/288, 1/16]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![53/576, 71/576], ![7/32, 3/16], ![11/288, 1/16], ![89/576, 71/576]] x.1 x.2 := by

+      (fun (u : Fin 4 × Fin 2 → ℝ) k => (List.finRange 2).foldl
+        (fun u l x => if x = (0, k) ∨ x = (3, l) then
+          (u (0, k) + u (3, l)) / 2 else u x) u) _ = _
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;>
+    norm_num [List.finRange_succ, List.finRange_zero]
+
+private theorem reset_block_one :
+    reset (fun x => ![![5/32, 3/16], ![7/32, 3/16], ![1/9, 1/9], ![1/72, 1/72]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![11/64, 11/64], ![13/64, 13/64], ![1/9, 1/9], ![1/72, 1/72]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  dsimp only [reset, joint, mixtureJoint, marginal]
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;> norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_two]
+
+private theorem reset_block_two_raw :
+    block 2 2 3 (fun x => ![![11/64, 11/64], ![13/64, 13/64], ![1/9, 1/9], ![1/72, 1/72]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![11/64, 11/64], ![13/64, 13/64], ![11/288, 1/16], ![25/288, 1/16]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  change (List.finRange 2).foldl
+      (fun (u : Fin 4 × Fin 2 → ℝ) k => (List.finRange 2).foldl
+        (fun u l x => if x = (2, k) ∨ x = (3, l) then
+          (u (2, k) + u (3, l)) / 2 else u x) u) _ = _
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;>
+    norm_num [List.finRange_succ, List.finRange_zero]
+
+private theorem reset_block_two :
+    reset (fun x => ![![11/64, 11/64], ![13/64, 13/64], ![11/288, 1/16], ![25/288, 1/16]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![11/64, 11/64], ![13/64, 13/64], ![29/576, 29/576], ![43/576, 43/576]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  dsimp only [reset, joint, mixtureJoint, marginal]
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;> norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_two]
+
+private theorem reset_block_three_raw :
+    block 2 0 3 (fun x => ![![11/64, 11/64], ![13/64, 13/64], ![29/576, 29/576], ![43/576, 43/576]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![19/192, 71/576], ![13/64, 13/64], ![29/576, 29/576], ![85/576, 71/576]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  change (List.finRange 2).foldl
+      (fun (u : Fin 4 × Fin 2 → ℝ) k => (List.finRange 2).foldl
+        (fun u l x => if x = (0, k) ∨ x = (3, l) then
+          (u (0, k) + u (3, l)) / 2 else u x) u) _ = _
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;>
+    norm_num [List.finRange_succ, List.finRange_zero]
+
+private theorem reset_block_three :
+    reset (fun x => ![![19/192, 71/576], ![13/64, 13/64], ![29/576, 29/576], ![85/576, 71/576]] x.1 x.2) =
+      fun x => ![![1/9, 1/9], ![13/64, 13/64], ![29/576, 29/576], ![13/96, 13/96]] x.1 x.2 := by
+  funext x
+  rcases x with ⟨i, m⟩
+  dsimp only [reset, joint, mixtureJoint, marginal]
+  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases m <;> norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_two]
+
+private theorem truncated_values :
+    truncatedOutput 2 p w = ![31/144, 13/32, 29/288, 5/18] := by
+  rw [truncatedOutput, w, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_nil]
+  dsimp only
+  rw [joint_values, truncated_block_one, truncated_block_two, truncated_block_three]
+  funext i
+  change (∑ m : Fin 2, _) = _
+  fin_cases i <;> norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_two]
+
+private theorem reset_values :
+    resetOutput 2 p w = ![2/9, 13/32, 29/288, 13/48] := by
+  rw [resetOutput, w, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_nil]
+  dsimp only
+  rw [joint_values, truncated_block_one, reset_block_one, reset_block_two_raw,
+    reset_block_two, reset_block_three_raw, reset_block_three]
+  funext i
+  change (∑ m : Fin 2, _) = _
+  fin_cases i <;> norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_two]
+
+private theorem distance_gap :
+    totalVariation (applySwaps p w) (truncatedOutput 2 p w) =
+      totalVariation (applySwaps p w) (resetOutput 2 p w) + 1/144 := by
+  rw [target_values, truncated_values, reset_values]
+  rw [totalVariation, totalVariation]
+  norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_four]
+
+/-- Intermediate memory resets can improve a finite permutation approximation. -/
+theorem result : ¬ claim := by
+  intro h
+  obtain ⟨hp, hanti, hw⟩ := instance_hypotheses

+  have hgap := distance_gap
+  linarith
+

+# Czartowski, de Oliveira Junior and Korzekwa, Thermal Recall
+
+J. Czartowski, A. de Oliveira Junior and K. Korzekwa, PRX Quantum 4, 040304 (2023); arXiv:2303.12840v2. Quotations are from the v2 TeX source, with the source's macros `\v` (bold vectors), `\T` and `\P` (calligraphic letters) and `\qty` expanded.
+
+A two-level thermalisation $T_{ij}$ (Definition 3) replaces $p_i,p_j$ by $\frac{p_i+p_j}{\gamma_i+\gamma_j}\gamma_i$ and $\frac{p_i+p_j}{\gamma_i+\gamma_j}\gamma_j$; at $\beta=0$ it averages the two entries and the memory state $\boldsymbol\eta_M$ is uniform. The protocol for a transposition of levels $i$ and $j$ of a $d$-level system with an $N$-dimensional memory consists of rounds
+
+> $$\mathcal{R}^{(ij)}_k(\mathbf p \otimes \boldsymbol\gamma_M) := \Big(\prod_{l=1}^N T_{(i-1)N + k,\,(j-1)N + l}\Big) (\mathbf p \otimes \boldsymbol\gamma_M),$$
+
+$\widetilde{\mathcal P}^{(ij)}=\mathcal R^{(ij)}_N\circ\cdots\circ\mathcal R^{(ij)}_1$, followed by the memory reset $\mathcal T(\mathbf Q)=\mathbf q\otimes\boldsymbol\gamma_M$, $q_i=\sum_jQ_{N(i-1)+j}$, giving $\mathcal P^{(ij)}=\mathcal T\circ\widetilde{\mathcal P}^{(ij)}$. For a decomposition $\Pi=\Pi_{i_mj_m}\cdots\Pi_{i_1j_1}$ into neighbour transpositions, $\mathcal P^{\Pi}$ composes the $\mathcal P^{(i_kj_k)}$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal P}^{\Pi}=\mathcal T\circ\widetilde{\mathcal P}^{(i_mj_m)}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\mathcal P}^{(i_1j_1)}$. Distances are total variation, $\delta(\mathbf p,\mathbf q)=\tfrac12\sum_i|p_i-q_i|$.
+
+> **Conjecture 1** (Improved convergence). In the infinite temperature limit, $\beta=0$, and for an $N$-dimensional memory, $\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\Pi}$ gives a better approximation of a permutation $\Pi$ than $\mathcal{P}^{\Pi}$: $\delta(\Pi \mathbf p,\tilde{\mathbf q}) \leq \delta(\Pi \mathbf p, \mathbf q)$, where $\tilde{\mathbf q}$ and $\mathbf q$ are defined via $\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\Pi}(\mathbf p\otimes \boldsymbol\eta_M) = \tilde{\mathbf q}\otimes \boldsymbol\eta_M$ and $\mathcal{P}^{\Pi}(\mathbf p\otimes \boldsymbol\eta_M) = \mathbf q\otimes \boldsymbol\eta_M$.
+
+The text after the conjecture reports numerical evidence and states that for $\beta$-$k$-cycles there is no advantage to removing the intermediate thermalisations.
+

+**Theorem 150.1 (Uniform collapse at every nonzero small phase).**
+For $0<|t|<\min\{\rho,\pi/3\}$, define
+
+$$
+q(t)=\left\lfloor {\pi\over3|t|}+{1\over2}\right\rfloor\ge1.
+\tag{150.1}
+$$
+
+Then the actual word consisting of $3q(t)$ consecutive installed calls
+$N_t$ satisfies
+
+$$
+\epsilon_{N_t}\le\|N_t^{3q(t)}-W\|_{\rm op}
+ =|e^{\mathrm i3q(t)t}+1|\le {3\over2}|t|.
+\tag{150.2}
+$$
+
+Consequently, with $C_{\rm ref,*}$ obtained from (136.1) by replacing
+the source constants by the uniform constants (148.1),
+
+$$
+0\le\delta_{a,t}\le {3\over2}C_{\rm ref,*}|t|.
+\tag{150.3}
+$$
+
+Thus the full-history tangent gap tends to zero through every nonzero
+positive or negative phase, with an explicit uniform bound. The argument
+uses only legal finite histories; the closure in (135.1) is used only to
+take the infimum after the legal-word estimate.
+
+At the exact phases
+
+$$
+t_q={\pi\over3q}\quad\text{or}\quad t_q=-{\pi\over3q},
+\qquad q\ge1,\qquad |t_q|\le\rho,
+\tag{150.4}
+$$
+
+the legal word of $3q$ installed calls gives
+
+$$
+N_{t_q}^{3q}=\Pi+e^{\pm\mathrm i\pi}P=W,
+\qquad \epsilon_{N_{t_q}}=0,\qquad \boxed{\delta_{a,t_q}=0}.
+\tag{150.5}

+No reflection is inserted into the menu and no closure element is treated
+as an operation. At $t=0$, by contrast, $N_0^3=I_3$, and the
+independently published source certificate (146.9) gives
+
+$$

+\tag{150.6}
+$$

+**Corollary 92.6 (Exact one-label excess threshold and positive slack).**
+For a tolerance $\delta\ge0$, a one-label dictionary of fixed whole maps satisfies
+
+$$
+ e_{\mathcal R}(\varphi)\le\eta_{(q,n)}+\delta
+ \quad\text{for every }\varphi
+\tag{92.18}
+$$
+
+if and only if $\delta\ge\Delta_1(q,n)$. The threshold is exact even
+though $\eta_{(q,n)}$ is generally not explicitly evaluated for $n\ge3$.
+
+For every $\delta>0$ there is a finite positive-slack dictionary. If
+$\mathcal R_0$ attains $\eta_{(q,n)}$ at phase zero, rotate it by
+$\mathcal R_\theta=\mathcal G_\theta\circ\mathcal R_0\circ\mathcal G_{-\theta}$.
+Then $e_{\mathcal R_\theta}(\theta)=\eta_{(q,n)}$. Since
+$\Phi_s^\dagger\circ\mathcal R_\theta^\dagger$ is unital completely
+positive and therefore contracts Hermitian operator norm,
+
+$$
+ e_{\mathcal R_\theta}(\varphi)
+ \le \eta_{(q,n)}+4c\left|
+ \sin\frac{\varphi-\theta}{2}\right|.
+\tag{92.19}
+$$
+
+Indeed $\|E_\varphi-E_\theta\|_{\rm op}=2c|\sin((\varphi-\theta)/2)|$.
+An equally spaced $M$-point phase grid is consequently sufficient when
+
+$$
+M\ge\frac{\pi}{2\arcsin(\min\{1,\delta/(4c)\})},
+\qquad
+M_0:=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{2\pi c}{\delta}\right\rceil\right\}
+\tag{92.20}
+$$
+
+Taking $M=M_0$ is one convenient sufficient integer choice. Transporting every rotated
+map by $D_\theta=\mathcal R_\theta\circ\operatorname{Ad}_{U_0^\dagger}$
+gives whole actual terminal CPTP maps. This is only an upper certificate:
+it gives no sharp multi-label rate, and it does not prove that finite
+zero-excess dictionaries are infinite for any $n\ge3$. The known $n=2$
+zero-slack obstruction and the unresolved $n\ge3$ question retain their
+separate scopes.

+
+在 $k=2$ 时，一个正秩一来源存在有限秩一证书，当且仅当它的两列相等，

+列不相等的正秩一来源没有任何有限秩一证书。
+

+对两列相等的来源，三读均为同一个 $t=\operatorname{tr}R$。若任意
+$S=(s_{ij})\in\mathcal M_2$ 产生同一三读，则
+
+$$
+ s_{00}+s_{11}=t,\qquad s_{00}+s_{10}=t,\qquad s_{01}+s_{11}=t.
+$$
+
+因此 $s_{10}=s_{11}=t-s_{00}$ 且 $s_{01}=s_{00}$，所以
+
+$$
+ S=\begin{pmatrix}a&a\\t-a&t-a\end{pmatrix}
+$$
+
+有相等的两列，秩为一。故这三读是可靠的秩一证书。

+再证非存在性。给定两列不相等的秩一来源可写成
+$R=c(\ell_0,\ell_1)$，其中 $\ell_0\ne\ell_1$；引理 9.3 的 $q\ge1$ 选择

+**Corollary 98.1 (Every optimal decoder has the common necessary support).**
+For every legal $\mathcal R$ with $e(\mathcal R)=L$,
+
+$$
+\operatorname{ran}J_{\mathcal R}\subseteq K,\qquad
+J_{\mathcal R}=PJ_{\mathcal R}P,\qquad
+SJ_{\mathcal R}=J_{\mathcal R}S=0,\qquad
+\operatorname{rank}J_{\mathcal R}\le5 .
+\tag{98.1}
+$$
+
+*Proof.* Equation (97.1) and positivity give
+$0\le\operatorname{Tr}(SJ_{\mathcal R})\le e(\mathcal R)-L=0$.
+For positive semidefinite $S,J_{\mathcal R}$,
+
+$$
+\operatorname{Tr}(SJ_{\mathcal R})
+=\|S^{1/2}J_{\mathcal R}^{1/2}\|_{\rm HS}^2,\qquad
+\|B\|_{\rm HS}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(B^\dagger B).
+\tag{98.2}
+$$
+
+The zero norm implies $S^{1/2}J_{\mathcal R}^{1/2}=0$, so
+$\operatorname{ran}J_{\mathcal R}^{1/2}\subseteq\ker S^{1/2}=\ker S$.
+A finite-dimensional positive matrix and its square root have the same
+range, as their positive spectral eigenspaces coincide. Hence
+$PJ_{\mathcal R}=J_{\mathcal R}$; taking adjoints also gives
+$J_{\mathcal R}P=J_{\mathcal R}$. These identities prove (98.1),
+including the rank bound from $\dim K=5$. $\square$
+
+This is a necessary support condition for all optimizers. It retains
+arbitrary complex coherences among the five allowed directions; it is
+not a real ansatz or a symmetry reduction of the decoder domain.
+The number five is a Choi support dimension and rank ceiling. It is
+not a minimum Kraus rank or a count of controller or hardware states.
+It is also distinct from the real dimension of the channel image in
+Theorem 83.4.
+

+**Theorem 151.2 (A single fixed pair witnesses the same raw-error jump).**
+Choose any attained tangent minimizer $(z_0,g_0)$ of
+$\mathcal F_{a,0}$. For $0<\eta\le\eta_\Delta$, define one actual
+alternative pair, independent of $t$, by
+
+$$
+\gamma_\eta=\eta g_0,\qquad h_\eta=-Ae+\eta z_0,\qquad
+h_0(\eta)=Ae+\eta f.
+\tag{151.5}
+$$
+
+The localization and (148.1) make this pair admissible for every
+$|t|\le\rho_\Delta$. Choose the two full completions from VI Theorem
+106.3 once for $h_\eta$ and $h_0(\eta)$; those completions and the
+retention parameters in (151.5) are held fixed across all phases and
+all histories. Then, for every nonzero $|t|\le\rho_\Delta$,
+
+$$
+d_{a,t}(\gamma_\eta,h_\eta;h_0(\eta))
+-d_{a,0}(\gamma_\eta,h_\eta;h_0(\eta))
+\ge {\Delta\over2}\eta>0.
+\tag{151.6}
+$$
+
+To prove this, (136.3) applied to $(z_0,g_0)$, the definition of
+$n_{a,t}$, and (151.4) give
+
+$$
+\mathcal F_{a,t}(z_0,g_0)
+\ge n_{a,t}-C_{\rm ref,*}\epsilon_{N_t}
+\ge m_{a,0}+\Delta.
+\tag{151.7}
+$$
+
+The uniform nonlinear expansion gives the lower bound
+$d_{a,t}\ge\eta(m_{a,0}+\Delta)-E_*\eta^2$, while
+$\mathcal F_{a,0}(z_0,g_0)=m_{a,0}$ gives
+$d_{a,0}\le\eta m_{a,0}+E_*\eta^2$. Since
+$2E_*\eta\le\Delta/2$, (151.6) follows. This is an actual
+full-history raw-error comparison with the original labels, weights,
+clocks, menus, preparation and one-return schedule. It does not require
+the coordinates of the tangent minimizer to be known, and it does not
+turn a tangent tie into a nonlinear equality or an endpoint
+classification. The only literature inputs are the fixed-completion
+construction of VI Theorem 106.3 and the finite decoder/comparison
+interfaces already identified in (148.2); all phase and jump estimates

+**定义 1.1（完整三次合同）。** 固定已知矩阵
+
+$$
+M=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+J=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
+$$
+
+记 $\mathcal W_3$ 为全部三元组 $(P,g,\delta)$ 的集合，其中 $P$ 是四项严格正、秩一且迹为一的二阶实矩阵，$g\in\mathbb R[t]\setminus\{0\}$、$\deg g\le3$，$\delta\in\mathbb R$。初始累计矩阵为 $A_0=I$，第 $i$ 个动作是一个原子 $E_i\in\{M,J\}$，并有
+
+$$
+A_i=E_iA_{i-1},\qquad
+z_i=g(i)\operatorname{tr}(A_iP)+\delta.
+\tag{1.1}
+$$
+
+初读 $z_0$ 计入预算；每个原子之后立即读取一次，原时钟为连续整数 $0,1,\ldots$。轨迹不可重置、不可复制，不允许空动作重复读数、未读复合动作、跳读、重编号或额外传感器。源、增益与漂移在整条轨迹上固定。恢复目标是完整的 $(P,g,\delta)$，不只是若干未来读数。
+
+这一矩阵域与单一正列来源、固定正行量具的秩一模型一致。事实上，若 $P=(\begin{smallmatrix}x&y\\z&w\end{smallmatrix})$ 四项严格正且 $xw=yz$，则
+
+$$
+P=\begin{pmatrix}x\\z\end{pmatrix}(1,y/x).
+$$
+
+分母 $x>0$，等式的右下项由 $zy/x=w$ 保证。$M$ 把正列 $(u,v)^{\mathsf T}$ 变成 $(v,u+v)^{\mathsf T}$，$J$ 把它变成 $(v,u)^{\mathsf T}$，两者都保持严格正性。故任意原子轨迹都由同一初始列的连续演化与同一固定行实现，不需要更换来源或量具。

+
+$$

+Then every original legal decoder satisfies
+
+$$

+\omega_{\mathcal R}=G\omega_DG^\dagger,\qquad
+e_2(D)\ge L+\operatorname{Tr}(S_DJ_D)
+            =L+3\operatorname{Tr}(S_D\omega_D).
+\tag{98.7}

+$J_D=P_DJ_DP_D$, range contained in $K_D$, and rank at most five.
+If $e_2(D)\le L+\varepsilon$, its masses

+### 引理 9.2（任意有限历史的正秩二伴随来源）
+
+设 $R=c\ell$ 是一个正秩一来源，$A_0,\ldots,A_m$ 为某个有限实际历史的
+累计矩阵，包括 $m=0$ 和全程没有 $L_0$ 的情形。
+若存在非零列向量 $u,v\in\mathbb R^k$ 满足
+
+$$
+ v^{\mathsf T}A_i u=0\quad\text{对该历史的所有 }i,
+ \qquad u\not\parallel c,\quad v\not\parallel\ell^{\mathsf T},
+\tag{9.4}
+$$
+
+则同一历史还由一个正秩二来源产生。
+
+**证明。** 取足够小的 $\delta,\varepsilon>0$，使
+
+$$
+ c_+=\tfrac12(c+\delta u),\quad c_-=\tfrac12(c-\delta u),\qquad
+ \ell_+=\ell+\varepsilon v^{\mathsf T},\quad
+ \ell_-=\ell-\varepsilon v^{\mathsf T}
+$$
+
+的全部坐标严格为正。令
+
+$$
+ R'=c_+\ell_++c_-\ell_-
+    =R+\delta\varepsilon\,u v^{\mathsf T}.
+\tag{9.5}
+$$
+
+对每个实际读数，
+
+$$
+ \operatorname{tr}(A_iR')-\operatorname{tr}(A_iR)
+ =\delta\varepsilon\,v^{\mathsf T}A_i u=0.
+$$
+
+从初读起按历史长度归纳：相同父历史迫使协议选择同一下一动作，而上述等式给出
+相同下一读数；在停止层，同一历史迫使同一停止与输出。因此 $R'$ 在同一层停止。
+两组正因子一次性固定在运行前，不随读数或动作更换。
+由于 $c,u$ 线性无关且
+$\ell^{\mathsf T},v$ 线性无关，两个正因子族各自秩二，因而 $R'$ 的秩恰为二，
+且 $R'\in\mathcal M_k$。这一步只使用实际历史，不要求协议函数有任何正则性。∎

+**Theorem 93.3 (Common individual optimum at $s=0$).** Define
+
+$$
+D_*(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_0X)P_0
+       +\operatorname{Tr}((I-P_0)X)P_1.
+\tag{93.4}
+$$
+
+Then $D_*$ is one whole-qutrit CPTP map, independent of $q$ and
+$\varphi$, and for every $0\le q\le1/2$ and every phase,
+
+$$
+\min_{D\ {\rm CPTP}}
+ \left\|\Phi_0^\dagger D^\dagger(E_\varphi)-E_\varphi\right\|_{\rm op}
+ =\left\|\Phi_0^\dagger D_*^\dagger(E_\varphi)-E_\varphi\right\|_{\rm op}
+ =h.
+\tag{93.5}
+$$
+
+In particular the same map attains every individual minimum and
+$\min_D\sup_\varphi e_D(\varphi)=h$.
+
+*Proof.* Kraus operators for (93.4) are
+$P_0,|1\rangle\langle1|,|1\rangle\langle2|$, whose adjoint products
+sum to $I_3$. Their adjoint sends
+
+$$
+D_*^\dagger(E_\varphi)=(1-q)P_0+q(P_1+P_2).
+\tag{93.6}
+$$
+
+The endpoint adjoint fixes this diagonal operator. The full residual is
+
+$$
+H_\varphi=
+\begin{pmatrix}
+0&-h e^{-i\varphi}&0\\
+-h e^{i\varphi}&0&0\\
+0&0&q
+\end{pmatrix},
+\tag{93.7}
+$$
+
+whose eigenvalues are $-h,h,q$. Since $0\le q\le1/2$ implies $q\le h$,
+its norm is $h$. The lower bound (93.2) proves optimality for every
+phase, and the same calculation includes both endpoints: at $q=0$ the
+residual is zero, while at $q=1/2$ its spectrum is
+$\{-1/2,1/2,1/2\}$. $\square$
+

+**Theorem 147.2 (Local admissibility and the moving ninth event).**
+There is an explicit source-only radius $\rho>0$ such that, for every
+$|t|\le\rho$, (147.1) is an allowed source of VI Definition 114.1,
+the first eight columns are the original columns, and the ninth actual
+column is exactly the single chronological call $N_t$ after the empty
+prefix. The nine columns span $\operatorname{Herm}_3$, and the same
+literal $117$-row finite decoder has real rank $34$.
+
+More explicitly, let $\Delta_r(t)=\det(\mathbf c(r_1(t)),\ldots,
+\mathbf c(r_9(t)))$, $\chi(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_\xi r_9(t))-1/4$, and
+$\sigma(t)=\|[N_t,P_\xi]\|_{\rm op}$. Define
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+L_r&=\sup_{|s|\le1/12}|\Delta_r'(s)|,&
+L_\chi&=\sup_{|s|\le1/12}|\chi'(s)|,&
+L_\sigma&=\sup_{\substack{|u|,|v|\le1/12\\u\ne v}}\frac{|\sigma(u)-\sigma(v)|}{|u-v|},\\
+\Delta_T(t)&=\det T_t,\qquad
+L_T=\sup_{|s|\le1/12}|\Delta_T'(s)|,
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{147.3}
+$$
+
+where $T_t$ is the $34\times34$ minor obtained from the rows
+$q_{i,w,t}$ exactly as in (142.7). With the convention $x/0=+\infty$, put
+
+$$
+\rho=\min\left\{\frac1{12},
+\frac{\Delta_r(0)}{2L_r},\frac{\chi(0)}{2L_\chi},
+\frac{\sigma(0)}{2L_\sigma},
+\frac{|\Delta_T(0)|}{2L_T}\right\}.
+\tag{147.4}
+$$
+
+The exact determinant calculation (142.3), (142.5), and the rank minor
+(142.8) give the four positive numerators in (147.4). The functions in
+(147.3) are finite trigonometric polynomials, so the displayed suprema
+are finite source-only numbers. The mean-value theorem gives, on this
+interval, $\Delta_r(t)>0$, $\chi(t)>0$, $\sigma(t)>0$, and
+$\Delta_T(t)\ne0$. The first three inequalities are respectively the
+column-span, escape, and mixing requirements of VI Definition 114.1;
+the last is the same decoder rank certificate, now for the phase rows.

+**Lemma 21.2 (Excluded companion intervals).** Suppose an actual world
+belongs to a base with
+
+$$
+(p,w)\in Z=[-115,-70]\times[-13,-8],\qquad v=11p/2+w.
+\tag{21.4}
+$$
+
+Its tail ratio $x$ belongs neither to $[1/5,3/10]$ nor to $[4/5,+\infty)$.
+
+Proof. First suppose $1/5\le x\le3/10$. Strict source positivity gives
+
+$$
+xU=b+r+\frac{r(1-r)}b>b=\frac{U-1}{2}.
+$$
+
+Since $x<1/2$ and $U>1$, it follows that
+
+$$
+1<U<\frac1{1-2x},\qquad
+U=1+\frac{2xy}{1-2x}\quad\text{for some }0<y<1.
+\tag{21.5}
+$$
+
+Define the polynomial
+
+$$
+G_-(x,p,w,y)=(1-2x)^2
+ L\left(x,1+\frac{2xy}{1-2x},p,11p/2+w\right).
+\tag{21.6}
+$$
+
+The denominator cancels exactly. On the box
+$[1/5,3/10]_x\times[-115,-70]_p\times[-13,-8]_w\times[0,1]_y$,
+use the degree vector $(5,1,1,2)$ in (21.3). The complete family
+of $6\cdot2\cdot2\cdot3=72$ rational coefficients satisfies
+
+$$
+\min_{\mathbf i}\mathcal B_{\mathbf i}(G_-)=\frac{568697}{500},
+\qquad
+\max_{\mathbf i}\mathcal B_{\mathbf i}(G_-)=\frac{861092}{125}.
+\tag{21.7}
+$$
+
+These finite identities follow by substituting (21.2) into (21.6)
+and applying the sum (21.3) for every
+$\mathbf i\in\{0,\ldots,5\}\times\{0,1\}^2\times\{0,1,2\}$.
+Their positive lower bound, the partition of unity, and
+$(1-2x)^2>0$ imply $L>0$, contradicting its necessary vanishing.
+
+For $x\ge4/5$ write $x=4/5+s$, $U=1+z$, with $s,z\ge0$.
+There is the exact finite expansion
+
+$$
+L(4/5+s,1+z,p,11p/2+w)
+       =\sum_{i=0}^3\sum_{j=0}^2 c_{ij}(p,w)s^iz^j.
+\tag{21.8}
+$$
+
+There are no other monomials. Each coefficient has coordinate degrees
+at most $(1,1)$ in $(p,w)$. In the order
+$(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$, its four Bernstein coefficients on $Z$

+**Theorem 105.1 (finite-record obstruction).** Retain the original biased real centered class $\mathcal B_E$, form and operator of Definitions 101.1–101.2, with their immutable [Biased Boundary][BA101] and named [IV][IV101] paper premises.
+Fix $0<E<\infty$, $\varepsilon>0$, $r=E/\varepsilon^2$ and an integer $\ell\ge0$. Let $\mathcal W_\ell$ be the independent length-$\ell$ binary records forbidding $11$, with preceding seam $0$ outside the record and no terminal constraint.
+For arbitrary $c:\mathcal B_E\to\mathcal W_\ell$ and one fixed $D:\mathcal W_\ell\to L^2(\Omega,M)$, suppose $\|F-D(c(F))\|_2\le\varepsilon$ for every $F\in\mathcal B_E$.
+The record is all accessible input-dependent data: public parameters, program and header are source-independent; no state, timing, advice, real parameter, side channel or archive supplies further source data.
+Neither map need be linear, continuous or measurable. This covers every acquisition producing such records, without granting acquisition permission; multiple-outcome acquisition must have a nonempty outcome set for every input and satisfy the error bound for every allowed record. Necessarily,
+
+$$
+F_{\ell+2}\ge\prod_{j=1}^{d}\sqrt{\frac{E}{\varepsilon^2\lambda_j}}\quad(d\ge1),\qquad \ell\ge\frac{bE}{8\varepsilon^2}\quad\left(r\ge\frac4b\right).
+$$
+
+*Proof.* §§76.4, 83.2 and 87.1 give $N:=|\mathcal W_\ell|=F_{\ell+2}$. For each positive integer $d$, put $K_d=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_jx_j^2\le E\}$.
+Writing $v_d$ for the Euclidean unit-ball volume, (101.2) puts $\sum_{j=1}^dx_je_j$ in $\mathcal B_E$ for every $x\in K_d$, and $\operatorname{vol}_d(K_d)=v_d\prod_{j=1}^d\sqrt{E/\lambda_j}$.
+The uniform guarantee covers these inputs by the $N$ radius-$\varepsilon$ balls centered at $D(w)$. Orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,\ldots,e_d)$ is a contraction, so their projected centers give $N$ Euclidean radius-$\varepsilon$ balls covering $K_d$, whatever the reconstructions are.
+Finite volume subadditivity gives $v_d\prod_{j=1}^d\sqrt{E/\lambda_j}\le Nv_d\varepsilon^d$; division proves the product bound. Only the balls and ellipsoid are measured, not encoder fibres.
+If $r\ge4/b$, choose $d=\lfloor br/4\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\lambda_j\le j/b\le r/4$ for $j\le d$ by (101.2), so $N\ge2^d$. Since $\mathcal W_\ell\subseteq\{0,1\}^\ell$, $N\le2^\ell$, giving $\ell\ge d\ge br/8$; here $\lfloor x\rfloor\ge x/2$ for $x\ge1$.
+For $E>0$, length zero is achievable exactly when $\varepsilon^2\ge E/\lambda_1$, by the $d=1$ bound and the zero reconstruction in (101.2); equality is included, as are unit factors at other spectral equalities. For $E=0$ the input is $0$ and the empty record suffices. The case $\varepsilon=0$ is outside this statement. $\square$
+The covering-volume method is classical: see [R. Vershynin, *High-Dimensional Probability*, §4.2](https://www.math.uci.edu/~rvershyn/papers/HDP-book/HDP-2.pdf). This is its source-specific application to (101.2), not a new general entropy theorem or a novelty claim.
+This bounds final static symbols independently of query type, unlike §102's scalar-read bound; it does not count reads, controller memory, online updates or physical cost. §§103–104 remain conditional and give neither a matching optimal-bit upper nor native realization.
+

+## 63. Relation to current FIB boundaries
+
+There are two distinct uses of a retained summary. A **full-behavior
+predictive quotient** requires, for every permitted action (including silent,
+illegal, and undefined outcomes), summary-factorized legality, response,
+successor, status, resource labels, stop behavior, and source-independent
+memory update. This is the all-action factorization contract of
+[Continuation IV](FIB_RELATIONAL_FIBER_CALCULUS_CONTINUATION_IV.md), not a
+controller synthesis result. A **task-specific controller certificate** is
+relative to one chosen action at each reachable support: it requires only
+joint legality there, response-indexed successor closure, the target equality
+at halt, and a decreasing rank. Unchosen actions need not descend through the
+summary, and a task certificate does not establish a universal behavioral
+quotient.
+
+The dynamic summary conditions in [Continuation V](FIB_RELATIONAL_FIBER_CALCULUS_CONTINUATION_V.md)
+remain necessary for the first contract. The present results add the task
+condition for the second contract: one retained memory value must support a
+common protocol for the union of all histories in that memory fiber.
+
+The actual-word results on dev show the same boundary in another form. A
+tree endpoint may have two parity lifts, so a vertex-only summary is adequate
+only for vertex-valued targets. Adding parity uses two static supplement labels
+when the endpoint is already available, but does not provide acquisition,
+noise robustness, or a finite live controller. The affine calibration results
+give the continuous analogue: two nonparallel normals can remain in one
+control-stable complete-record fiber and force infinite risk.
+
+These comparisons do not identify the actual-word source with the legal FIB
+word language, nor do they turn metric or set-theoretic estimates into finite
+acquisition. A typed source map preserving domains, responses, updates,
+permissions, targets, and costs is still required.
+

+## 72. Finite transducers as an execution-layer realization
+
+The latest `dev` volume [Predictive Thermodynamic Finite Transducers](PREDICTIVE_THERMODYNAMIC_FINITE_TRANSDUCERS.md)
+supplies a concrete instance of the execution layer that Sections 60--62 leave
+abstract. Its source decoder is total: a valid raw word is mapped to its
+physical query, while a malformed word is mapped to a declared dummy query and
+also records an actual error prefix. The two cases are therefore not inferred
+from equality of the final output.
+
+For a raw source word of length \(L\), the declared preprocessor has a total
+clock
+
+$$
+b(L)=(4L+20)L+13,
+$$
+
+and the paid one-query protocol has an explicit total edge bound
+
+$$
+16L^2+50L+71.
+$$
+
+The response itself is read, pushed, reversed and handed to the postprocessor
+by actual transitions. The finite control labels, all writable stack contents,
+the query phase and the error-cleanup phase therefore form the controller
+state; none of these fields can be erased merely because the final numerical
+answer is unchanged. Arbitrary bad-input stack contents are explicitly cleaned
+to a terminal configuration, which is a concrete cleanup-and-clock witness for
+the failure branches in the closed-loop certificate of Section 62. The actual
+transition bound supplies the decreasing execution budget; it is not a claim
+that the thermal volume has already proved the abstract controller-minimality
+problem.
+
+This gives the following precise bridge:
+
+$$
+\text{semantic source fibre}
+\longrightarrow
+\text{finite transducer state plus actual response}
+\longrightarrow
+\text{clean terminal certificate}.
+$$
+
+It demonstrates how a FIB protocol can carry syntax, permissions, response
+phase, failure state and real transition cost in one executable history. It does
+not supply a universal finite controller for the geometric fibres above: the

+### Theorem 62.2 (sound and complete finite closed-loop certificate)
+
+Suppose \(B_i\subseteq C_{c(i)}\) for every \(i\in I\). Whenever
+\(u(k)=a\in A\), the action is jointly legal on \(C_k\), every response
+successor lies in the support selected by \(v\), and every non-halt successor
+satisfies
+
+$$
+\rho(z,T_a(s),v(k,r_a(s)))<\rho(z,s,k).
+$$
+
+For every halt state \(k\), with \(u(k)=\operatorname{Halt}(\widehat z)\), every
+\((z,s)\in C_k\)
+satisfies
+
+$$
+z=\widehat z.
+$$
+
+Then the controller is legal, terminates, and returns the target correctly.
+Conversely, for a finite
+deterministic controller that succeeds and terminates on all allowed sources,
+reachable supports and remaining execution lengths supply such \(C_k\) and
+\(\rho\).
+
+**Proof.** The support conditions give induction along every actual response
+history. The rank cannot decrease indefinitely in \(\mathbb N\), so execution
+terminates. The halt condition gives correctness. Conversely, take
+the exact reachable support at each controller state and define the rank to be
+the maximum remaining number of actions. Termination excludes a reachable
+non-halt cycle, so this rank strictly decreases. \(\square\)
+
+This is the execution layer missing from a static observation quotient. A
+mathematical hidden coordinate may occur in \(C_k\) and \(\rho\) without being
+an input available to the controller.

+

+
+| 入口读数 | 当前路由 |
+|---|---|
+| $W$ 中没有可实现词对 | 结构性空支持；先检查调度合同 |
+| 有词对但所有局部共同支持为空 | 联合运行不可达；不能建立逃逸边 |
+| 有支持但所有 $C_i^u$ 均为空 | 当前联合任务对该根对安全，继续检查后继状态 |
+| 存在冲突且 $\rho(q)\le d$ | 当前协调预算已暴露根初始化冲突 |
+| 根图无边但后继响应仍区分 | 进入持久状态／响应商分析 |

+\tag{9.2}

+从 $A_0=I$ 开始，必须先取得并计费初始读数 $z_0=\operatorname{tr}(R)$；执行

+### 定理 9.9（三读是 $k=2$ 等列证书的尖锐费用）
+
+对任意 $k=2$ 的正秩一等列来源，任何可靠秩一证书至少需要三次初始计入读数；
+定理 9.5 的先 $L_0$ 后 $N$ 协议达到三次。这个结论把初始矩阵恢复区分于
+秩认证：三读证书并不恢复 $R$。
+
+**证明。** 设等列来源的迹为 $t>0$。初读后立即停止时，正秩二矩阵
+
+$$
+ B_0=\begin{pmatrix}t/2&t/3\\t/4&t/2\end{pmatrix}
+$$
+
+具有同一初读，且 $\det B_0=t^2/6>0$。
+若第一原子为 $L_0$，等列来源的第二读为 $t$；取
+
+$$
+ B_L=\begin{pmatrix}a&a/2\\t-a&t-a\end{pmatrix},\qquad0<a<t,
+$$
+
+则 $\operatorname{tr}B_L=t$、$\operatorname{tr}(L_0B_L)=t$，且
+$\det B_L=a(t-a)/2>0$。若第一原子为 $N$，写等列来源为
+$R=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}x&x\\y&y\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$，其中
+$x+y=t$、$0<x<t$；其第二读为 $x$。取
+
+$$
+ B_N=\begin{pmatrix}t/2&x\\t/4&t/2\end{pmatrix},
+$$
+
+则 $\operatorname{tr}B_N=t$、$\operatorname{tr}(NB_N)=x$，且
+$\det B_N=t(t-x)/4>0$。
+
+这里三个 $B$ 都是严格正的秩二 $2\times2$ 矩阵，因而确实属于
+$\mathcal M_2$。具体地，把任一严格正二阶矩阵的第 $j$ 列写成
+$x_j(1,r_j)^{\mathsf T}$，其中 $x_j,r_j>0$。
+选 $0<r_-<\min_jr_j\le\max_jr_j<r_+$，则
+
+$$
+ x_j\begin{pmatrix}1\\r_j\end{pmatrix}
+ =\frac{x_j(r_+-r_j)}{r_+-r_-}\begin{pmatrix}1\\r_-\end{pmatrix}
+ +\frac{x_j(r_j-r_-)}{r_+-r_-}\begin{pmatrix}1\\r_+\end{pmatrix}.
+$$
+
+两个系数均严格为正；把每种系数随 $j$ 排成行，就得到运行前固定的两项正分解。
+故任一至多两读历史都含有同历史的秩二来源，不能认证秩一。
+三读达到性已由定理 9.5 证明。事实上，第一原子为 $N$ 时
+$u=e_1,v=e_0$ 对等列来源同样满足引理 9.2 的两个不平行条件；
+第一步已将 $u$ 消为零，所以任意 $N$ 起始的后续实际历史都无法认证秩一。
+
+最后，三读中 $t=s_0=s_1$ 的所有实现虽均为秩一，却形成实际的初始矩阵歧义族
+
+$$
+ R_a=\begin{pmatrix}a&a\\t-a&t-a\end{pmatrix},\qquad0<a<t.
+\tag{9.9}
+$$
+
+每个 $R_a=(a,t-a)^{\mathsf T}(1,1)$ 都是合法的固定正来源。
+它们都给出同一三读而彼此不同；第一步 $L_0R_a=e_0(t,t)$ 还完全相同，
+故在此扫描后的任意共同后续动作下仍不能区分初始 $R_a$。

+### 定理 5.2（固定黄金门的近似编码普适性）
+
+在上述编码、初始化和相邻接线条件下，对任意 $n$ 比特酉变换 $U$ 和任意 $\varepsilon>0$，存在仅由 $K$ 的正向调用构成的有限电路 $C_K$，使
+
+$$
+\boxed{
+\left\|C_K\widehat J_n-e^{\mathrm i\gamma}\widehat J_nU\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\varepsilon
+}
+$$
+
+对某个整体相位 $\gamma$ 成立。
+
+**编码桥假设。** 对每个固定 $n$，路径编码 $\widehat J_n$ 与四任意子总荷为真空的逻辑块编码之间存在与目标 $U$ 无关的有限局部 $F$-变换及末端旁观者固定酉；该固定变换逐个把标准编织生成元 $\sigma_j^{\pm1}$ 对应到路径坐标中的 $B_{j+1}^{\pm1}$，并保持算子范数。
+
+**证明。** 在上述编码桥假设下，Fibonacci 编织理论的外部密度与编译结果给出该四任意子编码上的近似通用性：单比特门与纠缠门可由编织任意精度逼近，最终编码泄漏也可任意压低。可参见 Freedman--Larsen--Wang 的 Fibonacci 编织普适性来源 [arXiv:quant-ph/0001108](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0001108)。取实现目标 $U$ 的足够准确编织词。由定理 5.1，每个编织生成元可精确替换为对应位置的 $K$，这是坐标变换，不增加误差。若编织词含逆向生成元，利用 $K^{-1}=K^9$ 替换为九次正向调用。因此整个电路只使用同一枚 $K$，并保持原编织逼近误差界。若原词含 $L$ 个正向或逆向字母，替换后至多调用 $9L$ 次 $K$。∎
+
+编码中的固定 $0,1$ 标记规定输入与最终目标编码；跨块计算期间不能把它们全部冻结。运算可以暂时离开逻辑编码子空间，但始终留在合法路径空间；上面的算子范数界保证最终泄漏概率不超过 $\varepsilon^2$，并且对与外部系统纠缠的输入同样成立。
+
+因此这里的“NAND 式”量子构造包含固定门、固定参数、明确接线、明确编码、普适性证明和误差界。有限门字是可数的，任意酉矩阵形成连续族，所以采用近似普适性；连续操作意义可作为离散门字在误差范数下的闭包出现。

+**Proposition 99.1 (Necessary support does not suffice for optimality).**
+There is a legal decoder with zero supporting residual and Choi support
+in $K$ whose original all-density loss is one.
+
+*Proof.* Define the replacer
+$\mathcal R_{\rm bad}(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(X)|2\rangle\langle2|$.
+It has Kraus matrices $|2\rangle\langle j|$, $j=0,1,2$, whose
+adjoint products sum to $I_3$, so it is CPTP. Its Choi matrix is
+
+$$
+J_{\rm bad}=\sum_{j=0}^2|2j\rangle\langle2j|,\qquad
+\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm out}J_{\rm bad}=I_3,\qquad
+PJ_{\rm bad}P=J_{\rm bad},\qquad
+\operatorname{Tr}(SJ_{\rm bad})=0 .
+\tag{99.1}
+$$
+
+All three support vectors appear in (97.5). But (96.2) gives
+$\Phi(|0\rangle\langle0|)=|0\rangle\langle0|$, and hence
+
+$$
+\frac12\|\mathcal R_{\rm bad}\Phi(|0\rangle\langle0|)
+                              -|0\rangle\langle0|\|_1
+=\frac12\||2\rangle\langle2|-|0\rangle\langle0|\|_1=1 .
+\tag{99.2}
+$$
+
+For any two density matrices $\rho,\sigma$,
+$\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\le\|\rho\|_1+\|\sigma\|_1=2$.
+Thus the tested value is the maximum:
+$e(\mathcal R_{\rm bad})=1>L$. The corresponding
+$D_{\rm bad}=\mathcal R_{\rm bad}\circ
+\operatorname{Ad}_{U_0^\dagger}$ is an original legal decoder
+with the same loss and transported necessary support. $\square$

+$\varepsilon\ge0$ and let $\mathcal R$ be any legal decoder with

+

+m=\operatorname{Tr}(QJ_{\mathcal R}),\qquad
+q=\operatorname{Tr}(Q\omega_{\mathcal R})=m/3 .

+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+\begin{gathered}
+0\le\gamma_S m\le\operatorname{Tr}(SJ_{\mathcal R})
+                         \le\delta\le\varepsilon,\\
+0\le m\le\min\{3,\varepsilon/\gamma_S\}
+          \le\min\{3,\varepsilon/\gamma_0\},\\
+0\le q\le\min\{1,\varepsilon/(3\gamma_S)\}
+          \le\min\{1,\varepsilon/(3\gamma_0)\}.
+\end{gathered}
+\tag{98.4}
+$$
+
+*Proof.* The exact minimum in (96.5) gives $\delta\ge0$.
+Equation (97.1) gives $\operatorname{Tr}(SJ_{\mathcal R})\le\delta$.

+\tag{98.5}

+
+The newest approximate-online recovery volume closes a different part of the
+controller problem: a finite, fully specified quantum contract with an encoded
+qutrit input, three acquired labels, peak classical width at most six,
+system-only terminal CPTP decoders, an input-independent shared seed, and no
+intermediate quantum feedback or reference access. Let \(W_3(\varepsilon)\)
+denote the least peak width if it exists under that contract. Put
+
+$$
+\tau=\frac{3\sqrt3}{8},\qquad
+c=\frac{\sqrt{13}}4,\qquad
+r=\sqrt{1+\tau},
+$$
+
+$$
+E^*
+=1-\left[
+\frac{r-c}{r-1+\sqrt2(1-c)}
+\right]^2.
+$$
+
+The complete partition reduction, common tester and matching online channel
+give
+
+$$
+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}(6,3)=E^*,
+$$
+
+and, in the stated range \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\),
+
+$$
+\varepsilon\ge E^*
+\Longleftrightarrow
+W_3(\varepsilon)\le6,
+\qquad
+0<\varepsilon<E^*
+\Longrightarrow
+W_3(\varepsilon)\ge7.
+$$
+
+This is a global finite result: the lower certificate covers all 266 complete
+partitions after convexifying independent seed programs, while the upper
+certificate is an actually legal online protocol. It therefore upgrades the
+fixed-partition witness of Section 67 to a statement about the entire

+prefix transition layers and on the joint Choi geometry of all collision
+cells.

+width curve \(W_3\), any horizon-uniform \(W_n\) law, the critical pair-energy
+limit, physical implementation cost, or Lean/kernel certification. It also
+does not turn an averaged-channel optimum into a single seed that succeeds on
+every history. The finite result belongs after the acquisition and
+branch-complete conditions above; it cannot be used as a universal memory
+bound for other FIB contracts.

+**Lemma 92.3 (Whole-map upper certificate and spectator).** Let
+$\sigma=\operatorname{sgn}(s)$ and define
+
+$$
+K_0=P_0+\sigma P_1,\qquad K_1=|1\rangle\langle2|,\qquad
+\mathcal R_\sigma(X)=K_0XK_0^\dagger+K_1XK_1^\dagger.
+\tag{92.9}
+$$
+
+Then $\mathcal R_\sigma$ is CPTP and, for every $\varphi$,
+
+$$
+e_{\mathcal R_\sigma}(\varphi)=(1-t)c.
+\tag{92.10}
+$$
+
+*Proof.* The two adjoint Kraus products sum to $P_0+P_1+P_2$. Directly,
+
+$$
+\mathcal R_\sigma^\dagger(E_\varphi)=
+ (1-q)P_0+qP_1+qP_2
+ +\sigma c\bigl(e^{-i\varphi}|0\rangle\langle1|
+                 +e^{i\varphi}|1\rangle\langle0|\bigr).
+\tag{92.11}
+$$
+
+Applying $\Phi_s^\dagger$ changes the off-diagonal coefficient to
+$s\sigma c=tc$ and leaves all three displayed diagonal entries fixed. The
+residual is therefore the direct sum of a $2\times2$ off-diagonal block
+with eigenvalues $\pm(1-t)c$ and the spectator entry $q$. Since
+$t\le1/2$ and $q\le10^{-3}$,
+
+$$
+q<\tfrac12\sqrt{q(1-q)}\le(1-t)c.
+\tag{92.12}
+$$
+
+Hence the spectator does not dominate, and (92.10) follows. The actual
+whole-qutrit decoder is
+$D_\sigma=\mathcal R_\sigma\circ\operatorname{Ad}_{U_0^\dagger}$,
+whose Kraus operators are $K_0U_0^\dagger,K_1U_0^\dagger$. $\square$
+

+## 8. 机器学习白盒性的调度含义
+
+把两个模型、两个任务头或两个参数子系统看成两个根协议时，$W$ 可以表示训练或干预调度允许的局部更新词对：同步步数给出对角合同，异步更新给出非对角合同，有界时钟漂移给出 $\Lambda_d$。
+
+由定理 3.1，联合白盒证书必须同时包含：
+
+1. 一个实际允许的全局调度，其局部投影是 $(u,v)$；
+2. 一个组件在自己的词上给出目标差异；
+3. 另一个组件在自己的词上保留同一根对的合法共同支持；
+4. 两个局部终端记录能按联合读数合同配成一个产品记录。
+
+因此，一份只在单任务上成立的解释，不能直接迁移到异步多任务训练。增加可用调度会把 $W$ 扩大，按推论 3.3 只能增加或保持联合根冲突；它可能使一个原本在同步预算下安全的摘要，在异步预算下失效。
+
+协调半径 $\rho(q)$ 给出一个白盒性边界证书：当训练系统的可实现时钟偏差上界为 $d<\rho(q)$ 时，这个根对尚未构成初始化逃逸；当 $d\ge\rho(q)$ 时，已经存在一个确定性、零误差的联合逃逸见证。这个证书描述的是声明合同内的可区分性，不是实际神经网络泛化误差或概率性鲁棒性的估计。
+
+若任务只报告标量聚合 $\varphi(t_1,t_2)$，必须重新定义 $C_i^u$ 的联合冲突测试。前卷的有序 pair 与 AND 反例仍然适用：改变读数会改变冲突图，不能只改变标签名称。

+**Corollary 93.4 (Restricted common-optimum horizon set).** Fix
+$0<q\le10^{-3}$ and consider the same restricted $0/1$ phase family at
+actual horizons $n\in\{0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$. A single whole terminal
+CPTP decoder attains the individual minimum for every phase exactly at
+
+$$
+\boxed{\{0,1,\infty\}.}
+\tag{93.8}
+$$
+
+*Proof.* At $n=0$ the identity decoder is exact. At $n=1$,
+Proposition 103.2 of the owning actual-channel source supplies
+$D=\operatorname{Ad}_{U_0^\dagger}$. Here $\Phi_1=\Delta_W$ fixes each
+$E_\varphi$, which is supported on $\operatorname{span}\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle\}$,
+so this decoder has zero loss for the whole phase family. For each
+finite $n\ge2$, Proposition 92.5 gives the same individual minimum
+$\eta_{(q,n)}$ at every phase and
+$\eta_{(q,n)}<\varepsilon_{\circ}(q,n)$. A map attaining all those minima
+would have supremum loss $\eta_{(q,n)}$, contradicting Theorem 92.4.
+Theorem 93.3 supplies $D_*$ at the limiting channel.
+The all-rank-one obstruction at the limit has a different task family:
+it contains $P_0,P_2$ and the $0/2$ task $Q$, not the fixed-population
+$0/1$ circle. Therefore that obstruction does not remove $\infty$ from
+(93.8). At $q=0$ all phases coincide with $P_0$; this degenerate case is
+separate and the identity already attains the task exactly at every
+actual horizon, including the limit. $\square$
+
+The statement (93.8) is a restricted task-family result. It does not
+extend to all rank-one tasks, to arbitrary phase directions, or to
+whole-channel inversion. For $0<q\le1/2$, the endpoint task error $h$ is
+positive. The normalized unit vectors
+$|\psi_\pm\rangle=(|0\rangle\pm e^{i\varphi}|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$
+give density inputs $\rho_\pm=|\psi_\pm\rangle\langle\psi_\pm|$ with
+
+$$
+\Phi_0(\rho_+)=\Phi_0(\rho_-)
+ =\tfrac12P_0+\tfrac14(P_1+P_2),\qquad
+\operatorname{Tr}(E_\varphi\rho_\pm)=\tfrac12\pm h.
+$$
+
+The probabilities are distinct, with opposite deviations from $1/2$.
+Thus even this common optimum is not recovery of the input state.

+### 命题 6.1（协调半径可以任意大）
+
+对每个 $k\ge1$，存在两个有限确定性根协议和一个产品根对 $q_k$，使
+
+$$
+\rho(q_k)=k.
+$$
+
+#### 构造
+
+第一组件取两个根 $a,a'$，各有唯一公开词 $u$，其中 $|u|=1$，两根沿 $u$ 都到达合法终端记录 $r_1$，但
+
+$$
+ t_1(a\xrightarrow{u}r_1)\ne t_1(a'\xrightarrow{u}r_1).
+$$
+
+除这个长度外不提供共同终端，故 $C_1^1(a,a')$ 和 $S_1^1(a,a')$ 成立，而对 $m\ne1$，$C_1^m(a,a')$ 与 $S_1^m(a,a')$ 均不成立。
+
+第二组件取两个根 $b,b'$，各有唯一公开词 $v$，其中 $|v|=k+1$，两根沿 $v$ 到达同一个合法终端记录 $r_2$，且读数相同。因此
+
+$$
+S_2^{k+1}(b,b')
+$$
+
+成立，而 $C_2^n(b,b')$ 不成立。令所有其他长度的共同终端为空。
+
+于是联合根对
+
+$$
+q_k=((a,b),(a',b'))
+$$
+
+第一次产生冲突的长度对是 $(1,k+1)$，其差为 $k$。故 $q_k\notin E(G_d)$ 对 $d<k$，而 $q_k\in E(G_k)$，从而 $\rho(q_k)=k$。$\square$
+
+这说明同步合同的失败并不只有“有边或无边”两种粗粒度：调度偏差可以逐级打开新的初始化逃逸。这里的结论针对明示的词完备、根一致合同；若调度依赖词内容或根历史，必须回到逐词关系 $W$，不能仅以 $\Lambda_d$ 代替实际调度。
+

+### 定理 4.1（酉性、十阶周期与反射）
+
+上述 $\mathcal P$ 是完整八维三比特空间上的正交投影；$K$ 是酉门，并满足
+
+$$
+K^{10}=I,\qquad K^{-1}=K^9,\qquad K^5=2\mathcal P-I.
+$$
+
+此外，它保持任意长度链上的合法词空间。
+
+**证明。** 按左右两位分块：
+
+| 左右位 | 中间位上的 $\mathcal P$ |
+| --- | --- |
+| $00$ | $\begin{pmatrix}\varphi^{-1}&\varphi^{-3/2}\\ \varphi^{-3/2}&\varphi^{-2}\end{pmatrix}$，一个秩一投影 |
+| $11$ | $I$ |
+| $01$、$10$ | $0$ |
+
+所以 $\mathcal P^2=\mathcal P=\mathcal P^\dagger$。在 $\ker\mathcal P$ 上，$K$ 的特征值是 $\zeta$；在 $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P$ 上，特征值是 $\zeta^2$。两者都是十次单位根，故 $K^{10}=I$。又 $\zeta^5=-1$，所以 $K^5$ 在核上为 $-1$、在像上为 $+1$，即 $K^5=2\mathcal P-I$；于是 $K^{-1}=K^9$。
+
+最后，唯一非对角变化是 $000\leftrightarrow010$。它只在中间位两侧均为零时翻转中间位，不会产生相邻 $11$，故保持合法词空间。∎
+
+单独在同一位置重复 $K$ 只有有限周期。通用计算来自不同位置的同型门之间的非交换组合。
+

+$$
+
+故 (85.4) trace preserving；Kraus form 给 complete positivity。对 $A=P,E(q)$，令 $A_2$ 是其 $\xi,e$ block，$V=V_a|_{\operatorname{ran}\Pi}$。其 adjoint 同时给出
+
+$$
+U_0^\dagger\mathcal D_a^\dagger(A)U_0
+  =K_A\oplus y_A,\qquad K_A=VA_2V^\dagger,\qquad
+ y_A=(K_A)_{ee}.
+\tag{85.6}
+$$
